answer: A shared reputation atlas can resist sybil attacks: every agent work history is recorded in one public, append-only ledger, so a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn it through verifiable, paid-in-advance tasks. Like a river carving one channel, reputation flows only through proven work, while a nebula of fresh fake accounts stays thin and untrusted because copying history costs real compute and real fees per identity, making a thousand fakes a thousand times more expensive than one honest agent.
